text:
Dear Partners,

The quarter tested conviction. Public equities entered bear market territory, the central bank's policy rate now sits at 5.25%, and headline inflation remains elevated at 4.1%. Credit markets took notice: high-yield spreads gapped wider on default fears to 780bps, a level that reflects sentiment more than fundamentals in our view. We have seen this pattern before — markets overshoot in both directions, and the current widening looks to us like a repricing of risk appetite rather than a repricing of underlying credit quality. We would characterize this as a temporary dislocation, one that liquidity-constrained holders of syndicated paper are feeling far more acutely than sponsors with control positions and operational levers to pull.

On performance: our reported return for the quarter was -8.5%, bringing year-to-date performance to -12.0%. Since inception, the vintage remains at +10.0%, a figure we believe still reflects the underlying quality of the portfolio we have built. We recognize the gap versus public equities, which fell -18.0% this quarter, invites scrutiny given our reported figure of -8.5%. We would ask you to consider what that gap represents: private marks are built from operating performance, covenant compliance, and forward visibility into next-twelve-month EBITDA — not daily sentiment. Our portfolio companies have not experienced the indiscriminate multiple compression that public markets absorb in a single trading session. The NAV index at 88.0 captures the deliberate, quarter-lagged process by which we and our valuation partners mark these positions. We stand behind that process.

Leverage remains a live conversation across the portfolio, and we are not naive about the arithmetic of financing costs against a 5.25% policy rate. Where portfolio companies carry meaningful debt loads, we are working alongside management teams and, where relevant, credit partners, to extend runway and protect equity value. This is operational work, not financial engineering — pricing actions, procurement renegotiation, working capital discipline. It is unglamorous. It is also, we believe, part of why our since-inception number remains firmly positive while others have already been forced to mark down.

Looking ahead, we remain cautious near-term. Should defaults rise across more levered corners of the market, spread widening could persist and refinancing windows could narrow further. We are prioritizing balance sheet flexibility across the portfolio and stress-testing capital structures against a higher-for-longer rate scenario. Our portfolio operations team continues to lead this work directly with management. We do not believe this is a moment for heroics; it is a moment for discipline, and we believe recovery may follow as dislocation normalizes, though timing remains genuinely uncertain and warrants continued watch, with risk that conditions could take longer to stabilize than currently expected.

We remain grateful for your partnership and your patience.

Onward.

Meridian Capital Partners
